Welcome toWarming a Crystal

A crystal of two-level sites is warmed step by step — how many light up?

How would you like to begin?

Listen to the intro

About: Two-level systems in a crystal held at temperature T

Source

Concept
N = 400 two-level systems at fixed crystal sites, with levels at energy 0 and Δ (one state each), in thermal equilibrium at temperature T. f is the Boltzmann probability of the upper level. The grid lights N·f sites rounded to a whole number (the mean occupation, fluctuations left out); the bars show 1 − f and f on a fixed 0–1 scale; U/NΔ = f; C/NkB is the temperature derivative of U in units of NkB. Δ is held fixed and temperature is set and read as kBT/Δ.
Serves
Explaining how the heat capacity of a set of two-level systems depends on temperature, in terms of the populations of the two levels.
Inquiry
Six questions and a closing summary. Each uses the temperature slider or the Warm button (exactly +0.10 in kBT/Δ, counting the sites it lights) and shows, in the Readouts panel below the controls, only the readouts that question asks for.
Misconception
Probed through each question's answer choices; the feedback appears after a choice is made.

Pedagogy principles applied

PrincipleHow this sim honors it
Commit, then checkEach question is answered before it is checked in the sim; the readout it asks about is on screen only during its own question and reads — until you act.
No lookup leakThe energy and heat-capacity curves are drawn only across temperatures you have visited, and each question starts its traces afresh from its own starting temperature. Free Exploration opens with both curves drawn across the whole range.
Operational quantitiesWarm raises kBT/Δ by exactly 0.10 and reports the number of sites it lights; that number times Δ is the energy the crystal took in during the step.
Honest displayThe grid shows N·f rounded to whole sites; each site has a fixed random rank drawn once, so warming only lights further sites and cooling only darkens them.
Fixed scalesBars on a fixed 0–1 scale; both charts on fixed axes sharing kBT/Δ from 0 to 3.2, so nothing rescales while you explore.
Units statedTemperature as kBT/Δ, energy as U/NΔ, heat capacity as C/NkB; readouts to three decimals, with ×10 notation below 0.001 rather than a false zero.

Energy and heat capacity

Guided Inquiry

1 · The first warm step

The temperature starts at kBT/Δ = 0.10, where every site is dark. Press Warm once, which takes kBT/Δ to 0.20, and watch the grid. How many of the 400 sites become excited?

2 · A step at 0.40

The temperature is now kBT/Δ = 0.40. Press Warm once, which takes it to 0.50. How does the number of sites this step lights compare with the 3 lit by the step on card 1?

3 · Filling the upper level

Sweep the slider slowly from 0.50 up to 3.00, watching the two bars and the U/NΔ readout, which equals the upper fraction f. What happens to f?

4 · A step at 2.00

The temperature is now kBT/Δ = 2.00. Press Warm once, which takes it to 2.10. How does the number of sites lit compare with the 18 lit by the step from 0.40?

5 · Where C peaks

Sweep the slider slowly from 0.05 all the way to 3.00, watching the dot on the lower chart and the C/NkB readout. Where is the heat capacity largest?

6 · Doubling a high temperature

Read C/NkB at kBT/Δ = 1.50, then at 3.00. How does the heat capacity change when the temperature is doubled in this range?

7 · The Schottky peak

A crystal of two-level systems takes up heat well only when kBT is comparable with the gap Δ. Far below, e−Δ/kBT is tiny, almost no site can be excited, and C is close to zero.

Far above, the two levels are nearly equally filled, U levels off towards NΔ/2 and C falls as 1/T². In between C peaks: 0.439 NkB at kBT/Δ = 0.417.

This bump, the Schottky anomaly, is seen in real crystals holding two-level ions or impurities, on top of the heat capacity of the lattice itself, which this model leaves out.

Warming a Crystal of Two-Level Systems

✦Learn this with the AI tutor

01

At a glance

A crystal has 400 sites, and each site has two energy levels, a lower one at 0 and an upper one at Δ. The sim sets the temperature as kBT/Δ and shows how many sites are excited, the energy stored and the heat capacity.

What you'll learn

  • How the fraction of excited sites depends on kBT/Δ (notes, eqs. 5.29–5.30).
  • How many sites one Warm step lights.
  • Where the heat capacity is largest, and how it behaves at both ends (eq. 5.31).
The set-up: fixed sites, each with one lower and one upper level. A few are drawn.

What's on screen

  • Grid of 20 × 20 sites: a dark blue square is a site in its lower level, an orange one is in the upper level. A white ring marks the last Warm press's sites.
  • Bars beside the grid: the shares of sites in the lower level (1 − f) and upper level (f), on a fixed 0–1 scale.
  • Charts: U/NΔ (top) and C/NkB (bottom) against kBT/Δ, drawn over the temperatures visited, with a dot at the present one.
  • Readouts: temperature, excited sites, U/NΔ (= f), C/NkB and sites lit by the last Warm press.
See itShow the sim at its opening point, with both charts drawn in full. Watch for: every site dark blue, the lower bar full, and the dots at the left end of the charts.
02

Fixed: N = 400 sites in a 20 × 20 grid. Each site has a fixed place in a random order, so warming always lights the same sites in the same order. The grid shows round(400 f) sites, so a very small f can show none. The sim is an equilibrium picture and has no time dependence.

03

The upper level fills with Boltzmann odds and never passes half

A site has levels at 0 and Δ, one state each, so its partition function is Z = 1 + e−Δ/kBT (notes, 5.29). The two levels have probabilities 1/Z and e−Δ/kBT/Z.

Notes (5.29).

Let f be the probability of the upper level. The mean energy of one site is Δf (5.30). The sites are fixed and distinguishable, so ZN = ZN and U = NΔf. That is why the readout calls U/NΔ and f the same number.

Notes (5.30). Here ε is the mean energy per site.

The lower level has Boltzmann factor 1 and the upper has e−Δ/kBT, which is smaller at every finite temperature. So f stays below 1/2 and U below NΔ/2, however hot the crystal. At the opening point, kBT/Δ = 0.10, f = 4.5 × 10−5, and none of the 400 sites rounds to lit.

See itPark the temperature at the opening point, kBT/Δ = 0.10. Watch for: U/NΔ reading 4.54 × 10−5 and Excited sites reading 0 / 400.
See itRaise the temperature to the top of the range, kBT/Δ = 3.00. Watch for: U/NΔ reading 0.417, the upper bar still shorter than the lower one, and 167 / 400 sites lit.
04

One Warm step lights few sites when cold, most near the middle, and few when hot

Each Warm press raises kBT/Δ by exactly 0.10 and lights the extra sites. Pressed again and again from the opening point it lights 3, 11, 16, 18, 16 and 13 sites. Later steps light fewer: 2 from kBT/Δ = 2.00, and 1 by 2.90.

Sites lit by each Warm press, from the sim's own formula. The label under a bar is the kBT/Δ at which that press starts.

Each lit site carries energy Δ, so the sites lit by a step are the heat it took in, in units of Δ. The heat taken in per unit rise of temperature is the heat capacity C = dU/dT, which in these units is the slope of the U/NΔ curve.

C divided by NkB, in the sim's units.

A step of 0.10 therefore lights about 400 × 0.10 = 40 times C/NkB at its middle, and the count is rounded. The count follows the slope.

See itPress Warm once from the opening point, kBT/Δ = 0.10. Watch for: a white ring round a handful of sites, and Sites lit reading 3 (0.10 → 0.20).
See itPark at kBT/Δ = 0.40 and press Warm once. Watch for: a bigger ring on the grid, and Sites lit reading 18 (0.40 → 0.50).
See itPark at kBT/Δ = 2.00 and press Warm once. Watch for: just two sites ringed, and Sites lit reading 2 (2.00 → 2.10).
05

The heat capacity peaks at 0.44 NkB, near kBT = 0.42Δ

Differentiating U = NΔf with respect to T, with x = Δ/kBT, gives the heat capacity (notes, 5.31, drawn in Fig. 34).

Notes (5.31).

Its maximum is C = 0.439 NkB at kBT = 0.417Δ, where the U/NΔ curve is steepest. The notes quote “near 0.42Δ” and call a peak of this shape a Schottky anomaly. At that temperature f = 0.083, so about 33 sites are lit: the heat capacity peaks while the upper level is still sparse. At kBT = Δ it is only 0.197.

U/NΔ and C/NkB from the sim's formulas, over the range of its charts. The dashed vertical line marks the peak of C.
See itSet kBT/Δ to 0.42, near the peak. Watch for: the dot at the top of the C/NkB curve and the readout reading 0.439.
See itSet kBT/Δ to 1.00, where the thermal energy equals the gap. Watch for: the dot well down the falling side, and C/NkB reading 0.197.
06

The heat capacity falls away on both sides of the peak

Cold, the gap is large compared with kBT, so added heat can excite almost nothing (notes). C is small because e−x is. Hot, the two levels are already almost equally occupied, so more heat hardly changes the occupations. Either way U hardly moves.

The two limits of (5.31), by expanding for large and small x.

At kBT/Δ = 0.10, C/NkB = 0.0045, about a hundredth of the peak. In the hot limit, doubling the temperature cuts C by about four. In the sim, C/NkB goes from 0.100 at 1.50 to 0.027 at 3.00. The limit 1/4t2 gives 0.111 and 0.028.

Solid: C/NkB. Dashed: the cold limit x2e−x on the left and the hot limit 1/4t2 on the right, with t = kBT/Δ.
See itPark at kBT/Δ = 0.10, deep in the cold end. Watch for: C/NkB reading 0.005, with the dot at the foot of the curve.
See itPark at kBT/Δ = 1.50, then at 3.00. Watch for: C/NkB reading 0.100, then 0.027, a little over a quarter.
07

Where it matters

  • Paramagnetic salts. A spin in a magnetic field has two levels, so the heat capacity of a paramagnetic salt at low temperature shows this peak (notes, 5.3).
  • Atoms and defects. An atom with a low-lying excited state, or a defect in a crystal that can sit in either of two positions, is a two-level system. The sim's grid is such a crystal, one site per square.
  • A test for a gap. A heat capacity that is large only while kBT is comparable with a gap, and that dies away on both sides, points to a two-level structure.
Go deeper: entropy and limits of the sim

The notes give the entropy as S = NkB[ln(1 + e−βΔ) + βΔ/(eβΔ + 1)] (5.32). It rises from zero at T = 0 to NkB ln 2 at high temperature, which matches the count of 2N equally likely arrangements. The sim does not show it. It covers positive temperatures only. The notes add that spins can be prepared with more in the upper level, which gives a negative temperature and needs care.

08

Summary

In one line. Fixed two-level sites share energy with a heat bath, and this sim shows how many are excited and how the heat capacity changes as the crystal warms.

Key points

  • f = 1/(eΔ/kBT + 1) and U = NΔf, so f and U/NΔ stay below 1/2.
  • Sites lit by a Warm step ≈ 40 C/NkB: 3 from 0.10, 18 from 0.40 and 2 from 2.00.
  • C peaks at 0.439 NkB at kBT = 0.417Δ, a Schottky anomaly.
  • C vanishes at both ends: as x2e−x cold and as 1/4t2 hot.

Common mix-ups

  • “The same step in temperature always takes in the same heat.” The Warm step lights 3 sites cold, 18 near the peak and 2 hot.
  • “A hot enough crystal has most sites excited.” f is 0.417 at kBT/Δ = 3.00 and tends to 1/2 at most.
  • “C peaks when kBT equals the gap.” At kBT = Δ it reads 0.197. The peak is at 0.417Δ.

Things to try on your own

  • Find the temperature at which 100 of the 400 sites are lit, and compare it with Δ/(kB ln 3).
  • Press Warm from 0.10 upward and note where the counts stop growing.
